title: Client Mirror phase code vs pFedHN full-model generation
hypothesis: For client linear models whose personalized weights lie on a shared sinusoidal rank-2 orbit, a one-scalar client phase over a shared model basis will generalize to unseen clients and reduce total serialized server+client state versus a pFedHN-style full-model linear hypernetwork with two-dimensional client embeddings, while preserving client test MSE. A direct scalar phase code is the nearest simple control; equivalence to it means no Mirror-specific advantage. An off-orbit client may require a private residual.
physical_object: shared global 8-input/4-output linear model and two personalized weight directions
mirror_coordinate: one phase angle per client; client effects are generated by cos/sin action on shared matrices
logical_multiplicity: 64 in-orbit client models, including 16 clients with no local training examples, plus one off-orbit private client
controls: linear pFedHN-style hypernetwork outputting each full client matrix from a 2D client embedding
same hypernetwork with and without private off-orbit residual
Mirror phase code with and without private residual

development.selection_metric: unseen-client test nMSE, total serialized server+client bytes, communication bytes per client, generator MACs, private-state requirement

storage.authority: actual deterministic ZIP/NPY FP32 inference payload bytes after reload
paid_objects: all client embeddings or phase codes

success_gate: All fresh seeds: held-out unseen-client nMSE <=1e-5; total payload at least 20% below pFedHN-style generator+embeddings with no more than 1e-5 absolute nMSE increase; at least 10% below native scalar-phase code to claim Mirror-specific value; report off-orbit private residual and per-client communication.
failure_gate: Unseen-client nMSE exceeds 1e-5 on at least two fresh seeds; or Mirror saves <20% total bytes vs pFedHN; or native scalar phase is within 10% bytes and quality; or generation compute exceeds pFedHN by >2x.
development_decision: Both development worlds met unseen-client quality but the Mirror payload was only 11.7% and 13.8% smaller than pFedHN with private fallback, below the frozen 20% threshold. Native scalar phase is the same function and payload structure as Mirror; its metadata was corrected to match byte-for-byte before sealing. Record FAIL for the frozen margin and keep fresh seeds sealed; a different code/state protocol requires a new experiment.
amendment: Before fresh access, make the native scalar-phase control use identical inference arrays and execution metadata as Mirror, because both implement the same scalar coordinate map. No fresh results were accessed and no quality/byte threshold changed. Seeds 34111–34113 remain sealed after the development gate miss.
boundaries: synthetic post-fit federated linear regression, not trained federated neural networks
client phase attributes are available to both pFedHN and Mirror; no unseen client local samples are used for the in-orbit test
pFedHN control is a linear full-matrix hypernetwork specialized to a known sinusoidal task manifold, not a reproduction of the full pFedHN paper training stack
no optimizer updates; server bases are fitted by least squares from client training data
one deliberately off-orbit client is included to measure private-state need
